ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure A is a regional schematic diagram, marked near 40°N, and the river passes through place P; Figure B is an east-west geological section of the river valley at place P and its vicinity. In the figure, the left side is marked "west" and the right side is marked "east". The river valley section shows that the eastern bank is steeper, indicating that the eastern side is more strongly eroded. Then reason: Place P is located in the Northern Hemisphere; rivers in the Northern Hemisphere are deflected to the right under the influence of the geostrophic deflection force, and the right bank is more strongly eroded. In the figure, the strongly eroded bank is on the east side, indicating that the right side of the river's forward direction is the east side. When facing north, the right side is east; therefore, the flow direction of the river in Figure A is from south to north.
